package_info.why_malicious: Versions 2.0.5, 2.0.6, and 2.0.7 of the lottie-web package contain injected JavaScript code that, when loaded in a user's browser, automatically opens a popup to a crypto wallet phishing site. This behavior is unrelated to the package's legitimate purpose of rendering Lottie animations and constitutes a supply chain attack that puts end users at risk of credential theft and financial loss.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code opens a new browser window to 'https://connect-crypto-wallet.example.com' using window.open, causing an unsolicited popup to appear, which prompts the user to connect their Web3 wallet, potentially leading to credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code injects an unsolicited popup to an external crypto wallet site on any website using the package, which is not expected or required for an animation player library. The popup appears without user interaction and targets a domain unrelated to the package's functionality.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A Lottie animation player should only render animations and interact with the DOM for playback purposes. It should not open external browser popups or interact with cryptocurrency services, especially without user initiation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate crypto wallet browser extensions or decentralized applications (dApps) may open such popups to facilitate wallet connections, but a generic animation player like lottie-web has no valid reason to do so.
key_indicators: Unsolicited browser popup to an external crypto wallet domain
Reference to crypto wallet connection in a non-crypto-related package
Injected code executes on every page load without user interaction
window.open call with hardcoded phishing domain in animation player bundle

attack_chain.action: User visits a website that embeds the compromised lottie-web package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code in the package is loaded and executed in the user's browser.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes at runtime, opening a popup to a crypto wallet phishing site.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is prompted to connect their Web3 wallet, risking credential theft.

attack_chain.action: If the user connects their wallet, the attacker may gain access to the wallet or perform unauthorized transactions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential theft of cryptocurrency or sensitive wallet information.

behavioral_signatures: Animation player or web component package opening browser popups at runtime without user interaction
Presence of window.open calls to crypto wallet domains in non-crypto-related JavaScript bundles
Injected code that triggers on every page load regardless of user action
file_indicators: Unexpected code in dist/lottie-player.js or similar bundle files that opens external popups
Hardcoded references to external crypto wallet domains (e.g., connect-crypto-wallet.example.com) in package source
network_indicators: Outbound requests or browser popups to connect-crypto-wallet.example.com or other suspicious crypto wallet domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected browser popups or network requests to crypto wallet domains originating from animation or UI component packages. Scan package bundles for injected code that uses window.open to external domains or references Web3/crypto wallet APIs. Flag any such behavior in packages not intended for cryptocurrency use, especially if the code executes on every page load without user interaction.
